newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Chinese migrant-traffickers face Cambodian court.
newsitem.headline: Chinese migrant-traffickers face Cambodian court.

text.p: Proceedings will begin on Monday against five Chinese accused of trafficking in illegal migrants following police raids in Phnom Penh last week, a senior police official said on Sunday.

The alleged traffickers -- two from Hong Kong, three from China itself -- and their human cargo of 82 illegal migrants represented only the "tip of the iceberg" in a massive international network, the head of Cambodia's Interpol office, General M Ly Skadavy, told Reuters.
He said traffickers used Cambodia's weak rule of law to pass mainland Chinese on to the United States and Europe.
One of the Hong Kong citizens was wanted by the British colony's Interpol officials, General Skadavy said.
"He is known to traffic illegal immigrants from China to other countries," said the Interpol chief.

The involvement of the two Hong Kong citizens and three other ringleaders from China, together with "letters from Europe" found with the group provided clear evidence of an international trafficking racket, according to Skadavy.
He said there were as many as 10,000 illegal immigrants, mainly Chinese, in Cambodia, posing a serious problem for the government.
"We have our own economic problems, we don't need these people," he said.
Skadavy added: "We don't know how they are getting in without passports. It's possible they are coming by air."
He charged that corrupt Cambodian police officers were facilitating the illegal trade and called for a clean-up of the country's law enforcement system.

Chinese Embassy officials were not immediately available for comment. However Skadavy said that Cambodian authorities had received a go-ahead from the embassy to pursue charges against the arrested Chinese.
If found guilty they face deportation or prison sentences.
